thread.title: What Are The Recent Apple Supplier Warnings Telling Us About Apple - Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL)

author: Patient Tech Investor
title: What Are The Recent Apple Supplier Warnings Telling Us About Apple - Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL)
text:
News Timeline Beginning just a few trading days after Apple ( AAPL ) reported and guided its earnings on November 1, a string of several key Apple suppliers negatively updated guidance sending Apple and some suppliers in a downward spiral, a spiral that continues.
November 12th
It began with Lumentum ( LITE ), a supplier of parts for 3D sensing, for Apple ID recognition in newer iPhones. "We recently received a request from one of our largest Industrial and Consumer customers for laser diodes for 3D sensing to materially reduce shipments to them during our fiscal second quarter for previously placed orders that were originally scheduled for delivery during the quarter," The update reduced guidance from $405-430 million to $335-355 million.
November 13th
Next came Qorvo ( QRVO ) on November 13th. "Qorvo, a leading provider of innovative RF solutions that connect the world, today announced it expects revenue for the third quarter of fiscal 2019 to be in the range of $800 million and $840 million, compared to its previous forecast of $880 million to $900 million, due to recent demand changes for flagship smartphones." Smartphone sales in China were unchanged. In addition to its former business with Apple, Qorvo also won a major socket for the new iPhones which began shipping in September.
November 15th
One news article read , "Austria's AMS ( AMS ), which makes facial recognition technology, became the latest Apple supplier to cut its revenue forecast," continuing, "The new AMS guidance suggested between 11 and 18 million fewer iPhones would be produced in the fourth quarter than an initially estimated 77-82 million, Credit Suisse analysts said in a note to customers." AMS re-guided to between $480 million and $520 million from $570-610 million.
Prior
Other Apple suppliers, British chipmaker IQE ( IQE ) and screen maker Japan Display guided down.
Up to this point, the common thread for the weak guidance was heavy exposure to new iPhones. Even Dialog Semiconductor ( DLGS ), "said late on Wednesday it does not see a drop in demand from Apple. Dialog justified this by pointing out that it supplies many more products than the latest iPhones."
Discussing The Meaning Hidden in this list of warnings resided several important conclusions. Left from most of the news was Apple's $390 million investment in Finisar (NASDAQ: FNSR ) for producing 6" wafers needed in 3D applications. "Apple is accelerating the investment at the second source supplier to diminish its risk." Needham & Co analyst Alex Henderson said. On November 9th, this announcement hit the news, "II-VI Incorporated to Acquire Finisar, Creating Transformative Strategic Combination with Leading Positions in Photonics and Compound Semiconductors."
The massive Lumentum cut cratered Apple and many of its key suppliers. Approximately half of Lumentum's revenue was from Apple. With the help of some math, the approximate $75 million drop in revenue calculates into a 35% reduction, a drop just days after Apple's guidance. Regardless of the fact that Lumentum's content was in newer phones, the cut was huge. Although Lumentum in a later meeting with UBS claimed that the update was from inventory and not market share loss, other analyst didn't necessarily agree, "Assuming Finisar has about 20% share of the overall 3D sensing market and II-VI has 10% share, this is likely roughly a 33% reduction in demand across the entire segment," said Alex Henderson, a Needham analyst in a report. "With Lumentum accounting for 70% of 3D sensing, we think the company is taking on the full brunt of the impact."
Regarding Qorvo, former news revealed that it would gain a significant socket in the new iPhone XR. In early 2018, Qorvo announced a major design win with a tier one customer. With the announcement came commentary. "Qorvo's design win at Apple would secure a lucrative socket that has been held by Broadcom Ltd. (NASDAQ: AVGO ) for the past two generations," the analyst said. This could result in $230 million to $305 million in incremental revenues for Qorvo in the second half of calendar 2018" The company guided close to $900 million for December before the cut from the approximately $840 million in the previous December quarter. Before the major design win, approximately 40% of its revenue came from Apple representing $340 million. Making an assumption that the additional $60 million of revenue guided for this year's December, Qorvo expected roughly $400 million from Apple. The company cuts its guidance approximately $50 million mid-range to mid-range or 12%. A drop of 12% for the December quarter could represent 8-10 million phones. We should note: Broadcom ( AVGO ) believes it will win back the lost socket.
According to analysts, AMS's represented approximately 15 million phones.
Before December, three suppliers cut its forecasts by 10 to 25 million phones. One of the key suppliers, Dialog held guidance claiming a broad based access with Apple. The common thread with the warners was heavy or sole exposure in new Apple products. Was this a sign about product mix or was there a deeper issue? The answer came on December 3.
The Cirrus Warning The night before its latest conference call, Cirrus Logic ( CRUS ) updated its guidance cutting $60 million or at our average ASP number of $4.85 10-15 million units in line with Qorvo and AMS. Apple uses Cirrus in virtually every product except watches. Apple's iPhone unit sales is lagging; it's now very clear. But how much?
The Effect on Apple Results We wrote an article, Cirrus Logic's Perfect Storm, which included a section on Apple's recent inventory management change for Cirrus'. Apple did change it drastically to generally a quarter by quarter from its previous method year by year. Since Apple's phones have the greatest effect on Cirrus's revenue, we can calculate approximate changes using the following factors: Apple is 85% of Cirrus' revenue; Apple sells approximately 15 million units of computers and tablets per quarter at ASPs averaging $2; and without the dongle Cirrus' average, ASP is somewhere near $4.85. Cirrus in the past has tried to guide with the top range $10-20 million under its expected revenue. Beginning with the September quarter, calculating the number of delivered iPhone units is 370 million times 0.85 minus ($2 times 15 million) divided by $4.85 equals approximately 60 million units. Apple sold 47 million in the September quarter leaving 13 million extra in inventory. For December guidance given on November 1st of $400-$360 million, the iPhone calculation is $410 million times 0.85 minus ($2 times 15 million) divided by $4.85 equaling approximately 65 million units. For December guidance given on December 3rd of $340-$300 million, the calculation is $350 million times 0.85 minus ($2 times 15 million) divided by $4.85 equals about 55 million units. Notice the slightly different number of iPhones units calculated by the two different approaches, 10 million versus 12 million.

With the updated guidance dropped the number to 65-70 million in line with the lowered revenue guidance from both Qorvo and AMS. With what appears to us for Apple's quarter by quarter inventory management, we believe that iPhones sales are significantly lower than last year and will be ranged between 65 and 70 million. We think that the major warning from Lumentum is from allocation changes not reflecting sales. We expect this lower trend to continue. Yes, it is still possible that Apple was keeping higher inventories for all suppliers. We just don't believe so especially with the large corrections it made with Cirrus in the March and June quarters.
